title: Allocator bulkhead and KV journal heal for GPU OOM and fragmentation escalations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customer escalations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments surfaced a correlated pattern: sustained small allocations from session arenas combined with delayed KV cache journal flushes produced long-lived fragmentation and periodic GPU OOM waves. Symptoms included tail latencies, elevated eviction churn, and tenant-specific OOM spikes that persisted despite node restarts.

Root cause hypothesis: The runtime allocator allowed a few noisy sessions to grow their per-session arenas without backpressure; concurrently the KV cache journal writer stalled under IO contention in some environments (notably on certain on-prem storage backends), causing higher in-memory tombstone density and preventing timely compaction. The combination amplified external fragmentation and prevented the GPU memory reclaim path from freeing contiguous blocks quickly, triggering OOMs.

Proposed fix: 1) Introduce an allocator bulkhead: per-session arena cap plus a soft throttling policy to prevent runaway session expansion; 2) Implement a KV journal "heal" background worker that performs incremental CRC checks, tombstone pruning, and opportunistic compaction without blocking foreground reads/writes; 3) Add an adaptive eviction bias that prefers large-span consolidation when fragmentation metrics exceed threshold; 4) Expose a feature flag to enable the full flow for canary clusters and a runtime knob for journal flush aggressiveness.

Expected impact: Reduced frequency of tenant-specific OOM waves, lower eviction churn, and improved long-tail latency. The patch is designed to be safe for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private we will provide a benign default and documented knob because some storage backends require different tuning.
resolution_plan: 1) Code: allocator bulkhead + journal-heal worker + eviction bias implemented in branch feat/allocator-bulkhead-journal-heal (PR in review). 2) Tests: add unit tests for arena cap enforcement and simulated journal stall; add an integration test that injects tombstone floods. 3) Canary: enable on 2 Dedicated clusters and 5% of Hosted traffic with feature flag for 72h. 4) Rollout: progressive rollout to remaining Dedicated and Hosted nodes if canary metrics (OOM rate, eviction rate, p99 GPU memory usage) improve by >= 60%. 5) Private customers: provide opt-in advisory and a small patch bundle that adjusts journal flush backoff for on-prem storage.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Incident triage: Aisha P. documented initial customer reports (Hosted: corp-app-prod; Dedicated: tenant-alpha; Private: legal-corp). Noted correlation with high tombstone counts in KV index and long-lived session arenas.

2026-03-02 - Repro: Miguel O. created a stress harness that simulates frequent small allocations and a delayed journal writer; reproduces fragmentation and OOM within ~90 minutes on a 4-GPU node (internal kube env).

2026-03-03 - Analysis: SRE observed that journal fsync latency spikes on some Private customer images (NFS variant). Added diagnostic counters for journal lag and per-session arena growth. Linked logs to the incident page.

2026-03-04 - Prototype: Eng implemented a bulkhead cap for arenas (soft cap with throttling) and a first-pass journal healer that scans a bounded window and schedules compaction tasks; preliminary tests reduce OOM rate in harness by ~70%.
2026-03-06 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6242 - includes allocator bulkhead, journal heal worker, and feature flag. Requesting review from memory team and SRE.

2026-03-07 - Canary plan approved by PM/Execs. Metrics to watch: OOM count, eviction rate, p50/p95/p99 token latency, journal-lag histogram. Dashboard created: https://dash.redwood-inference.internal/d/runtime/oom-frag-1009999
2026-03-08 - Canary start: Enabled feature on dedicated-canary-2 and hosted-canary-5. Early telemetry shows drop in new OOMs and a 35% reduction in eviction churn after 6h.

2026-03-09 - Observation: One Private customer still saw intermittent OOMs due to extreme NFS fsync latency. Added specific guidance for Private: set journal_flush_backoff_ms to 250 and enable journal-heal feature flag; performing remote debug with customer infra.

2026-03-10 - Code review and minor refactor: moved healing worker to lower-priority thread group to avoid interfering with token-critical fast paths. PR updated with tests. Planning rollout to 50% after signoff.
follow_ups: Add end-to-end regression in CI that simulates journal stalls and validates healing completes without service impact
Extend observability: per-tenant fragmentation heatmap and tombstone-age distribution
Document Private deployment tuning matrix for common storage backends (NFS, EBS, SMB)
